source.title: Loss Landscape Degeneracy and Stagewise Development in Transformers
source.authors: Jesse Hoogland; George Wang; Matthew Farrugia-Roberts; Liam Carroll; Susan Wei; Daniel Murfet

record.tranche_reason: The study trains a new two-layer attention-only language model and tracks previous-token attention, prefix matching, and relative loss by token position using measures aligned with the original induction-head work.
record.gate_note: The text reports results measuring induction-circuit structure and in-context learning in a two-layer language model. It does not directly test whether the induction circuit is causally necessary or sufficient, nor does it report a training-loss bump aligned with induction-head formation. The one-layer experiment does not report induction-head measurements.
record.test_reason: The study trains a new two-layer attention-only transformer on Pile text, the architecture of the original work. It tracks K-composition, previous-token matching, prefix matching and the ICL score (loss at token 500 minus token 50) across training. These results bear directly on the induction mechanism (V1), its timing against in-context learning (V2) and whether formation happens in sub-steps (V7). Induction heads are not the paper's main focus, which is LLC-based stage division, but the measures follow Olsson et al.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right but incomplete. The paper's main conclusion is that LLC-defined stages coincide with structural and behavioural changes, suggesting degeneracy and development are linked. Within that, the two-layer LM learns bigrams (LM1), then n-grams and positional use (LM2), then previous-token heads (LM3), then induction heads with an ICL-score drop (LM4). Head composition begins in LM2. The authors present these as case studies, not universal phenomena.
record.recipe_differences: Uses aligned head-composition, previous-token matching, prefix-matching, and relative-token-loss measures in a new training run on a subset of the Pile; it does not report a direct causal intervention on the circuit.
record.method_sensitivity: The authors state that stage boundaries depend on checkpoint spacing, smoothing, the choice to differentiate by training time or log time, and the plateau tolerance. Structural induction-head results are reported for the two-layer language-model run.

fits_no_version.finding: Loss-landscape degeneracy (LLC) changes mark the induction-circuit stages. The LLC falls in LM3 (Δλ̂ −1.57) and rises in LM4 (+8.62), with stage boundaries at 6.5k, 8.5k and 17k steps.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Induction-circuit formation sub-steps coincide with distinct changes in local learning coefficient (degeneracy).

record.problems: The induction-head structural analysis is centered on one two-layer model run; additional seeds are used to examine LLC stage divisions, not to reproduce the structural analysis. The authors do not establish a causal link between degeneracy and development. The text does not report a training-loss bump aligned with induction-head formation, and several plotted measurements are presented without numerical values in the text.
record.rows_left_out: No otherwise relevant reported results were left out. The one-layer language-model experiment reports early bigram, positional-embedding, and n-gram changes but no induction-head measurements, so it does not supply rows for the tested versions.

untested.parts: A bump in the loss curve at induction-head formation is not reported for the two-layer model. Abruptness is not quantified beyond stage boundaries.
All of it; no large models are studied.
Structural induction measures come from one run. Five extra seeds are checked for LLC stages only, not head metrics.
Data and training setup are not varied for the language model.
Few-shot task learning is not separated from copying.

missing.what: Per-stage test-loss changes for the two-layer LM (LM3 −0.18, LM4 −0.40). These are relevant to whether a loss bump accompanies induction-head formation.
missing.locator: Figure 1a table; Appendix B.2, Figure B.1

missing.what: LLC stages LM1–LM4 recur in five seeds, but head metrics were not recomputed across those seeds.

record.verdict_notes: The one-layer model's loss bump (Appendix E) is unrelated to induction heads, since one-layer models cannot form them. All head-metric values are figure-only. Tranche could arguably be T3, because the LLC framing is new, but the induction measures match the original.

versions.untested_parts: Tests composition and attention-pattern measures, plus an illustrative copying-related prediction change, in one two-layer attention-only language-model run. It does not establish causal necessity or sufficiency, and does not test the mechanism across a broad set of models.
Tracks induction-related head measures and relative token-position loss during training. It does not establish a precise onset window or report a training-loss bump at the same time.
The study does not test whether induction heads explain most in-context learning in large transformers.
The structural induction-head analysis is not repeated across model families, sizes, modalities, or independent training runs.
The study does not vary language-model training data or setup to test their effect on induction-head formation or persistence of in-context learning.
The study does not distinguish few-shot task learning from repeated-token copying or compare induction heads with other few-shot-learning mechanisms.
Tests the temporal ordering of previous-token-head and induction-head measures in the studied language-model run; it does not establish whether all models undergo the same sequence.

rows.measure: ICL score: loss at token 500 minus loss at token 50; more negative indicates better relative later-token performance

rows.note: The study describes previous-token heads rising over LM3 and induction-head prefix matching increasing during LM4, alongside the ICL-score drop.
rows.check: The ICL-score drop co-occurs with induction-head prefix matching in LM4 (8.5k–17k of 50k steps). No loss-curve bump is reported: Figure 1a gives a stage test-loss change of −0.40 for LM4 and −0.18 for LM3. So the bump part of V2 is not shown by this row.

relationships.condition: single two-layer attention-only LM run (~3.4M params, Pile subset)
relationships.reason: Induction heads 2:7 and 2:8 K-compose with first-layer heads 1:2 and 1:5 (R1–R4). Those heads become previous-token heads (R5–R6), 2:7/2:8 gain prefix matching (R7–R8), and repeated-token prediction improves (R9). No causal ablation was run.
relationships.display_finding: Heads 2:7 and 2:8 developed key composition with heads 1:2 and 1:5 as previous-token attention, prefix matching, and repeated-token prediction improved, without causal ablation.
